name: Umbrella Academy Car Stare
core: Vanya stares from one car and Five stares back stunned from another; used for two parties awkwardly noticing each other in the same situation.
avoid: Not for warm, friendly reunions.

name: Yes Dear
core: A cheerful woman makes a request and a worn-out face answers with weary compliance; used for tired, resigned agreement.
avoid: Not for enthusiastic agreement.

name: We Have It At Home
core: Kid asks for something, mom says we have it at home, and the home version is a sad knockoff; used for disappointing cheap substitutes.
avoid: Not for substitutes that are actually better.

name: Now That's A Name I Haven't Heard In A Long Time
core: Obi-Wan wistfully recalls an old name; used when something long forgotten is suddenly mentioned again.
avoid: Not for brand-new things.

name: Dafuq Did I Just Read
core: Samuel Johnson squints at a paper then looks up appalled; used after reading something baffling or absurd.
avoid: Not for sensible, clear writing.

name: Church Gun
core: A man sits unaware while two women behind him quietly draw guns; used for an oblivious target and the threat sneaking up on it.
avoid: Not for real violence or attacks on places of worship.

name: WTF Face
core: A guy grimacing in disgusted confusion; used to react to something gross or baffling.
avoid: Not for pleasant surprises.

name: Spiderman Presentation
core: Spider-Man presents in front of a projector screen; used to share a 'fact' or hot take as if it's an official lecture.
avoid: Not for multi-part dialogue.

name: Mr Krabs Money
core: Mr. Krabs rolling blissfully in a pile of cash; used for the joy of finally getting paid or getting something you crave in abundance.
avoid: Not for losing money or being broke.

name: Thousand Yard Stare
core: A shell-shocked soldier staring blankly into nothing; used for feeling traumatized or numb after an ordeal.
avoid: Not for real war tragedies or genuine trauma.

name: Girl Putting Tuba on Girl's Head
core: One girl calmly placing a tuba over another girl's head; used when someone or something smothers you with an unwanted thing while you just stand there.
avoid: Not for mutual or welcome situations.

name: Loading Cat
core: A frozen cat with a loading spinner on its face; used when someone (or something) needs a long time to process what just happened.
avoid: Not for quick, sharp responses.

name: Breaking Bad Smile Frown
core: Hank grinning wildly beside Hank scowling; contrasts what makes you happy with what makes you miserable.
avoid: Not for things that are equally good or bad.

name: This Little Maneuver Is Gonna Cost Us 51 Years
core: Interstellar astronaut realizing a quick decision will cost decades; used when a small shortcut or mistake turns out to have huge time costs.
avoid: Not for decisions with no lasting consequence.

name: You Wouldn't X A Y
core: Parody of the anti-piracy ad 'You wouldn't steal a car'; used to mock an overblown moral argument with an absurd comparison.
avoid: Not for sincere public-service messages.

name: Plate Toss
core: One guy serves another a plate, who instantly flings it away; used when an offer or gift is rejected immediately.
avoid: Not for offers that get accepted.

name: Run
core: An orangutan on a tricycle chasing a screaming girl; used for being pursued by something you desperately want to escape.
avoid: Not for welcome or friendly encounters.

name: Kevin James
core: Kevin James with a sheepish, smug grin and hands in pockets; used when you've done something mildly embarrassing and own it.
avoid: Not for genuine remorse or anger.

name: Redditor's Wife
core: A woman gazing sadly at her partner hunched over a glowing computer; used to describe someone neglecting their partner for the internet.
avoid: Not for happy couples sharing screen time.

name: Vein Forehead Guy
core: A teen straining with a bulging forehead vein; used for desperately holding something in, like laughter or a comment.
avoid: Not for relaxed, carefree moments.

name: Blank Yellow Sign
core: A blank yellow warning sign; used to post a mock warning or notice about something.
avoid: Not for scenes needing a person or reaction.

name: High Drunk Guy
core: A bleary-eyed, grinning guy who looks totally wasted; used for absurd 'deep' thoughts or dumb ideas that sound genius in the moment.
avoid: Not for sober, sensible advice.

name: Pathetic Spidey
core: Batman and Iron Man shower cash on a poor Spider-Man scrambling for it; used when the well-off flaunt resources at someone who has none.
avoid: Not for equal footing between parties.

name: Monkey Business
core: A chimp in a shirt typing at an office cubicle; used for clueless work or someone faking competence on the job.
avoid: Not for genuine expertise.

name: We Have A Hulk
core: Loki boasts 'I have an army' and Tony Stark coolly replies 'We have a Hulk'; used to answer a big threat with an even bigger trump card.
avoid: Not for situations where you're outmatched.

name: No Yes Lady
core: A woman grimacing in disgust, then reconsidering with intrigue; used when something seems bad at first but grows on you.
avoid: Not for things you hate consistently.

name: Borat
core: Borat grinning with two thumbs up; used to celebrate a (often dubious) success with 'Great success!'.
avoid: Not for failures or sad news.

name: Gordon Ramsay Some Good Food
core: Gordon Ramsay savoring a dish with the subtitle 'Finally, some good food'; used when something finally meets your standards after a run of bad ones.
avoid: Not for criticism or disappointing results.

name: Jessica Jones Death Stare
core: Kilgrave leaning in and staring intently at an uncomfortable Jessica Jones; used when someone or something creepily fixates on you.
avoid: Not for mutual affection.

name: DBZ Fusion
core: Goten and Trunks doing the fusion dance and becoming Super Saiyan 3 Gotenks; used when two things combine into something far more powerful.
avoid: Not for things that combine badly.

name: Chill Out Lemur
core: A lemur holding up a calming palm; used to tell someone to calm down about something overblown.
avoid: Not for encouraging excitement.

name: Nobody Expects The Spanish Inquisition
core: Monty Python's red-robed inquisitors bursting in; used for something showing up completely unexpectedly.
avoid: Not for planned or predictable events.

name: Urinal Guy
core: A man picks the urinal right next to the only other guy despite a whole empty row; used for someone choosing the most awkward option when plenty of space exists.
aliases: picks the urinal next to you
avoid: Not for situations where space is genuinely scarce.

name: I Said We Sad Today
core: A guy leaning into a friend's face insisting 'I said we sad today'; used to force someone to share your gloomy mood.
avoid: Not for genuinely cheering someone up.

name: Love Actually Sign
core: Mark silently confessing via cue cards at the door in Love Actually; used for a heartfelt or awkward confession delivered via sign.
avoid: Not for loud, spoken announcements.

name: Spongebob My Eyes
core: Patrick screaming 'My eyes!' with bloodshot eyes; used when you see something painful, bright, or horrifying.
avoid: Not for pleasant sights.

name: Sisyphus
core: Sisyphus endlessly pushing a boulder uphill; used for a pointless, never-ending task.
avoid: Not for tasks that actually get finished.

name: Mario Hammer Smash
core: Paper Mario slamming a hammer down; used for crushing or forcefully dealing with something.
avoid: Not for gentle or careful handling.

name: Joey Repeat After Me
core: Phoebe coaching Joey to repeat a phrase until he confidently gets it wrong; used when someone keeps failing to learn something simple.
avoid: Not for someone who learns quickly.

name: Borat I Go To America
core: Borat leaving his village joyfully as the crowd watches; used for excitedly heading off somewhere or leaving something behind.
avoid: Not for reluctant or sad departures.

name: Multi Doge
core: A wall of countless Doge faces; used for something overwhelming in quantity or everywhere at once.
avoid: Not for single, rare things.

name: If I Had A Nickel For Every Time
core: Doofenshmirtz: 'If I had a nickel for every time X, I'd have two nickels... which isn't a lot, but it's weird it happened twice'; used for an oddly specific thing that happened exactly twice.
avoid: Not for things that happen constantly.

name: I Declare Bankruptcy
core: Michael Scott shouting that he declares bankruptcy, used when someone tries to escape a huge problem with a dramatic, useless announcement.
avoid: Not for real financial hardship or serious debt stories.

name: Advice Yoda
core: Yoda gives advice in his backwards Yoda grammar, used for wise-sounding tips with inverted word order.
avoid: Not for advice that doesn't work in Yoda's inverted sentence style.

name: Penguin Gang
core: A crew of rockhopper penguins strutting together, used for a group showing up as a squad to deal with something.
avoid: Not for solo reactions; it needs a group showing up together.

name: Scared Hamster
core: A hamster frozen in open-mouthed shock, used for sudden fear or alarm at something small.
avoid: Not for calm or happy reactions.

name: Yeah If You Could
core: Bill Lumbergh from Office Space passive-aggressively asking for something unreasonable, used for bosses making annoying requests.
avoid: Not for genuine, polite requests.

name: Eric Andre Let Me In
core: Eric Andre desperately shaking a locked gate and screaming to be let in, used for being shut out of something you badly want.
slots: the place or thing they're locked out of
avoid: Not for situations where someone gets in easily.

name: Trump Interview Papers
core: An interviewer squints in confusion at papers he's handed, used when someone presents baffling evidence as if it proves their point.
avoid: Not for evidence that actually makes sense.

name: Godfather
core: Don Corleone shrugging with open hands, used to complain that someone asks a favour without respect, or to make an offer they can't refuse.
avoid: Not for real threats or violence.

name: Kirby Holding A Sign
core: Kirby cheerfully holds up a blank sign, used to deliver any wholesome or blunt message with cute enthusiasm.
avoid: Not for long messages; the sign is small.

name: Karen
core: The asymmetric bob haircut that stands for an entitled person demanding to speak to the manager, used for petty complaints.
avoid: Not for reasonable complaints or attacks on real private people.

name: Joins The Battle
core: The Super Smash Bros. new-challenger splash, used to announce someone or something unexpected entering a situation.
avoid: Not for things that were already part of the situation.

name: Is Mayonnaise An Instrument
core: Patrick earnestly asking if mayonnaise is an instrument, used for a sincerely dumb question in the 'Is X a Y?' format.
avoid: Not for smart or reasonable questions.

name: Uncle Sam I Want You
core: Uncle Sam pointing at the viewer, used to recruit or call out the reader for some task or duty.
avoid: Not for messages not aimed at the viewer.

name: The More You Know
core: The NBC PSA shooting-star logo, used to sarcastically present a useless or obvious fact as enlightening.
avoid: Not for genuinely important safety information.

name: Robert Downey Jr Eye Roll
core: Robert Downey Jr. rolling his eyes with arms crossed, used for exasperation at something said for the hundredth time.
avoid: Not for genuine surprise or delight.

name: Powerpuff Girls Creation
core: Professor Utonium's recipe of sugar, spice, everything nice and accidental Chemical X, used to list the ingredients of something with one chaotic extra.
avoid: Not for things without a recipe-like list of ingredients.

name: I Find Your Lack Of Faith Disturbing
core: Darth Vader force-choking an officer who doubted him, used to menacingly respond to someone doubting your favourite thing.
aliases: i find your lack of faith disturbing
avoid: Not for friendly disagreements with no menace.

name: Brace Yourselves
core: Ned Stark gravely warning that something is coming, used to predict an incoming flood of annoying, predictable things.
avoid: Not for events that already happened.
